# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## SpreadsheetBench scorer semantics (grounded in evaluation.py, not yet RESULT-confirmed)
- Cells compared via openpyxl `data_only=True`. `transform_value`: int/float → round(float,2);
  str → round(float(str),2) if numeric else kept; `datetime.time` → str(v)[:-3] (trims to
  HH:MM); `datetime` → Excel serial rounded to whole days. Then `type(v1)!=type(v2)` fails.
- Implication 1: a number stored as TEXT ("42") MATCHES a real number (both → float). So
  "numbers as strings" is NOT a failure here — do not write a rule against it.
- Implication 2: a date/time written as a STRING fails, because the real value is trimmed/
  serialized while the literal string is compared verbatim. Write real datetime/time values.
- Implication 3: an answer_position range with no "!" is graded on the FIRST sheet
  (sheetnames[0]); a named sheet must match exactly.
- Promising but not yet tried: for persistently flaky multi-cell ops (sort, dedup), a worked
  copyable code snippet likely beats prose for this mid-strong reader (gemma-4-31B).
